devto.title: We Didn't Invent New AI Architecture. We Rediscovered 20-Year-Old Computer Science.
devto.description: The AI industry isn't inventing a new paradigm. It is frantically rediscovering classical computer science from 20 years ago.

devto.title: The Dataset Was Lying: 4 of 6 "False" Facts Were True
devto.description: We red-teamed our own memory-verification experiment: 4 of 6 'false' trap facts were true, the conclusions inverted, and the real fix for temporal claims was a verb tense.

devto.title: Went down a rabbit hole testing whether LLMs can actually verify agent memory claims on their own. Turns out the evidence format matters way more than the model — bare token strings barely work, real code context changes everything.
devto.description: Bare tokens vs real code: an 11x recall jump in LLM memory verification (3400 calls, 14...

devto.title: Bare tokens vs real code: an 11x recall jump in LLM memory verification (3400 calls, 14 models)
devto.description: 14 models, 4 arms, ~3400 API calls. No model balanced false-accept and recall with pattern strings. With real file snippets: recall 0.08→0.88 at FA=0.02. The problem was the evidence, not the model.

devto.title: I turned my portfolio into an MCP server (and I'm not a programmer)
devto.description: A civil engineer who directs AI agents built a portfolio that answers questions from other AI agents. Here's what broke, what worked, and why.

devto.title: The Mechanical vs. The Semantic: What Happens When AI Memory is Wrong?
devto.description: An empirical look at memory contamination in AI agents. I ran an experiment to see how agents handle false facts, tested a retraction mechanism, and closed the final gap with verify-on-read.

devto.title: What I learned building a long-lived AI agent (the boring version)
devto.description: A practical log of building a long-lived Telegram AI agent — caching, providers, routing, memory, latency. No benchmarks. Just what actually happened.
